chunks: When Ziyād read the letter, he said, "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, he has testified to it." This remained in his mind until Mu'āwiyah claimed him (as his brother by his father).

key_terms.ادَّعَاهُ: He claimed him (specifically in the context of lineage or brotherhood).
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Ka'bah, the sacred house in Mecca, often used in oaths.
key_terms.زِيَادٌ: Ziyād, referring to Ziyād ibn Abihi, a prominent companion and governor.

ai.seo_question: What was Ziyād's reaction when he read the letter regarding his lineage?
ai.summary: Ziyād ibn Abī Bakr’s oath 'by the Lord of the Kaaba' highlights his pragmatic acceptance of Mu'awiyah’s political maneuvering to legitimize his rule through familial ties, a key theme in the transition from the Rashidun to the Umayyad era. This moment underscores the tension between Ziyād’s known lineage and Mu'awiyah’s strategic adoption of him, reflecting the broader Shia critique of political expediency over divine right.
